source_context_translations.translation: The Way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
Without name, it is the beginning of Heaven and Earth; with name, it is the mother of the myriad things.
Therefore, one should constantly be without desire in order to observe its subtle mystery.
One should constantly have desire in order to observe its border.
These two come forth together but are named differently; together they are called the profound.
Profound upon profound: the gate of all subtle wonders.
When all under heaven know beauty as beauty, then ugliness has already appeared.
When all know good as good, then what is not good has already appeared.

Thus being and nonbeing give birth to each other, difficulty and ease complete each other, long and short compare with each other, high and low incline toward each other, sound and voice harmonize with each other, and front and back follow each other.
Therefore the sage handles affairs without action,
and carries out teaching without words. The myriad things arise, and he does not refuse them; he gives birth to them but does not possess them; he acts but does not rely on his own strength;
When his work is accomplished, he does not dwell on it.
Precisely because he does not dwell on it, it does not leave.

He does not exalt the worthy, and so the people do not contend; he does not value hard-to-get goods, and so the people do not become thieves; he does not display what is desirable, and so the people's minds are not thrown into disorder.
Thus in the sage's governance, he empties their minds and fills their bellies,
weakens their wills and strengthens their bones.
He makes the wise dare not act.
If one acts by nonaction, then nothing will not be governed.

The Way is empty, and when used it is perhaps never filled; so deep, it seems like the ancestor of the myriad things. It blunts its sharpness, unties its tangle, tempers its brightness, and mingles with its dust; so deep, it seems perhaps to exist.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A physical route or passage along which one travels.
Sentence Translations (English): There is a broad road ahead, and carts and horses may travel on it.
He entered the mountains by the path and did not lose his way.
The guest asked for the road, and the boy pointed to the west gate.
Traveling by night, he lost the path and then turned back home.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A way of doing something, especially a practical approach, procedure, or technique.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Emphasizes practical procedure rather than a physical route.
Sentence Translations (English): There is a proper method for governing the state, and then the people are at peace.
Each craft has its own method, and it must not be mixed up.
In learning, what matters is to grasp the right method.
Warfare also has its method, and it does not rely on force alone.
Sentences: 工巧各有其道，不可亂也。

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To utter or state something verbally, or to talk about it explicitly.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Used for verbal expression, not for naming as a label.
Sentence Translations (English): I do not dare to speak of the details.
Do you want to speak of this matter?
The classic text does not fully say so.
All spoke of its beauty.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The fundamental guiding principle, order, or path that structures reality and human conduct.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this context it names the absolute, underlying Way rather than a road, method, or verbal act of speaking.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text in the received Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Used predicatively to judge something as fitting, proper, or worth doing.
Sentence Translations (English): This proposal is indeed acceptable.
His remarks are worthy of consideration.
The time is not yet ripe, so it is still not suitable.
This plan is the most workable.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To agree to something or give it approval.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Volitional or judgmental assent, not mere capability.
Sentence Translations (English): I approved what you requested.
The opinions were not unified, and in the end it was not approved.
When the master heard the plan, he gave his approval.
The ruler had already approved his memorial.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Expresses ability, possibility, or permission for an action to be done.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks possibility or capability rather than evaluation.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Used to mark something as mistaken, improper, or not right.
Sentence Translations (English): His remark was completely wrong.
This action was very improper.
To take this as right is in fact mistaken.
Losing what is correct is a great error.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Negates the following predicate or noun phrase, asserting nonidentity or exclusion.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this text it negates the noun phrase that follows.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The enduring, unchanging Way as a fixed principle.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Names the Way as permanent and not subject to ordinary change.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text in the received Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To give something a name or explicitly call it by a term.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Requires an act of naming or designation.
Sentence Translations (English): The father named the son.
I dare to name it.
When the mountains and streams were fixed, they then named the place.
All the mouths together named the affair.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Publicly known standing or renown, whether good or bad.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Covers reputation in society, not a literal label.
Sentence Translations (English): A gentleman values his reputation.
After a long time, he gained fame.
His reputation was already well known, and near and far all knew it.
Wealth and rank are not worth valuing; only reputation is hard to preserve intact.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A word or designation by which something is identified or called.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it is the label or designation itself, not the act of naming.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text in the received Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A fixed, enduring designation that does not change.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Emphasizes permanence of naming rather than the act of naming itself.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text in the received Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A philosophical notion of lack of determinate being, or the state of being void of things.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Abstract metaphysical sense, not simple negation.
Sentence Translations (English): The myriad things arise from nothingness.
The sage keeps to nonbeing in responding to things.
To know being and nothingness is then to see their completeness.
Emptiness and stillness are close to nonbeing.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Negates possession or presence; marks that something is absent.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this context it contrasts the absence of a name with the presence of a name.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; early philosophical layer preserved in the received Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The paired totality of heaven and earth, often referring to the natural world as a whole.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A set binomial for the whole cosmos, not two separately focused nouns here.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A third-person object pronoun referring back to a previously mentioned person or thing.
Sentence Translations (English): I saw him in the courtyard.
Once one has obtained it, one does not lose one’s hold.
You may ask him.
I have never abandoned it.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A verb meaning to go toward or arrive at a place.
Sentence Translations (English): I shall go east.
Tomorrow I will go to Chu.
The boat may go to the river.
Where do you wish to go?

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Links a modifier to the noun it qualifies, forming a genitive or attributive relationship.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks possession, attribution, or nominal linkage.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To commence an action, process, or state.
Sentence Translations (English): When a matter is about to begin, one should be cautious.
When spring thunder had sounded, the farming work began.
After the state became chaotic, government reforms only then began.
They sat and discussed matters deep into the night, and only then was it settled to begin.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The point from which something starts or comes forth.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Names a source point or first stage, not the act of beginning.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Used before a noun to indicate an unspecified but real quantity or instance.
Sentence Translations (English): There is a tiger in the mountains.
There is a lamp inside the room.
There were some people of the time who knew this.
There is an old well in this place.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks possession or existence, indicating that something is present or available.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Existential or possessive presence, opposed in context to 無.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; early philosophical layer preserved in the received Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The totality of created or existing things in the world.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Collective philosophical sense, not a count of exactly ten thousand items.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A woman in the role of parent.
Sentence Translations (English): A mother teaches her child with ritual.
A kind mother loves her child.
After losing his mother, his cries were very sorrowful.
His mother was in the hall.
Sentences: 母教子以禮。」「慈母愛其子。

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A source or origin compared to a mother who gives birth and nourishes.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Metaphor for source or generative origin in this text.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces a conclusion, inference, or result from what has just been said.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks an inferential transition from premise to conclusion.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Happening many times or at repeated intervals.
Sentence Translations (English): I often go there.
A worthy man is usually sparing of speech.
This matter is often seen in history.
The human heart often easily changes.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Continuing without interruption or lapse over time.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks habitual or enduring continuity.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To feel or express desire for something.
Sentence Translations (English): All people desire to live.
What do you wish to do?
I do not wish to say much.
The gentleman wants it to succeed.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A wish or craving directed toward obtaining or doing something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Refers to appetitive longing, especially the kind to be quieted or reduced.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces the means, basis, or instrument used to carry out an action.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it introduces purpose or means, not comparison or cause.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To look at or observe something visually.
Sentence Translations (English): He ascended the tower and looked out.
The crowd watched the battle together.
I stood and watched it.
He watched the fish by the water.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To look at attentively in order to understand, inspect, or perceive.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Directed, reflective seeing rather than casual looking.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Used demonstratively to point to a thing or group already identified.
Sentence Translations (English): I took that one.
I saw that man and questioned him.
He loved that virtue.
Few are those who know that heart.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A third-person possessive or attributive pronoun referring to something already mentioned.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Possessive reference to an antecedent.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Delicately profound, fine beyond ordinary perception, and difficult to fully grasp.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it describes an elusive subtlety rather than overt brilliance.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The limit or edge where something ends or is marked off.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A limit or margin, not a measuring instrument or a boundary line in a technical sense.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A demonstrative referring to something near at hand or immediately under discussion.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Points to something present in discourse or context.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The number 2, or a pair.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Counts exactly two entities, often as a pair.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A nominalizing suffix or marker used after a quantifier or pronoun to form a noun phrase referring to a person or thing.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Creates a category of entities rather than asserting action.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates identity, sameness, or acting together as one.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Focuses on sameness or shared action.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To go forth, issue from, or become visible.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Movement or emergence outward.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Connects clauses or phrases, often indicating sequence, continuation, or contrast.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Flexible connective with broad syntactic linkage.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Not the same as what was just mentioned.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks difference or nonidentity.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To refer to something by a certain term or description.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Predicative naming or designation.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Deep, elusive, and beyond ordinary clear explanation.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Suggests depth and obscurity rather than mere darkness.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Adds repetition or intensification, indicating one more step or occurrence.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Can mark recurrence or added degree.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A large number of people or things taken together.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Collective plurality.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): An opening or entrance used for access or passage.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Physical entrance, also used figuratively for an entry point.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The realm of human society or the whole world under heaven.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Political-cosmological totality, not merely the globe.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Including every member without exception.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Universal quantification.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To perceive, recognize, or understand something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Cognitive awareness or understanding.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A person or thing regarded as beautiful.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Concrete noun use, not merely the quality.
Sentence Translations (English): Everyone loves beauty.
The beauty of the mountains and waters is worth appreciating.
His words had beauty in them.
Outwardly beautiful, but substantial within.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Pleasing in appearance or character, or the quality of such pleasingness.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Can denote the quality or the beautiful thing itself.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To treat one thing as another, or to regard something in a certain way.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Predicative identification or interpretation, not causation.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks the resulting conclusion or immediate consequence.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Signals a direct result from the preceding statement.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To feel aversion toward someone or something.
Sentence Translations (English): All detested it.
I greatly disliked his words.
All together hated oppressive rule.
A gentleman does not dislike learning because of poverty.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Morally or socially bad, harmful, or undesirable.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Negative evaluation, often contrasting with good.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates that something has come to completion or that a state has already been reached.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks completion or settled fact.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Morally right, beneficial, or of good quality.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it names or qualifies what is morally good.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Negates the following word or phrase.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): General verbal or adjectival negation.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates reciprocal relation or action between the items linked to it.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks mutual or reciprocal interaction.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To cause something to come into being or appear.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Causative emergence or generation.
contextual_sense.Translation (English): to give rise to; to produce

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The paired opposites of difficulty and ease.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A fixed opposed pair.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To bring something to completion or make it into something through interaction or support.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Completion through reciprocal relation, not merely finishing.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The paired opposites of length and shortness.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A fixed contrast pair.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To place side by side in order to judge relative degree or difference.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Evaluative comparison, often by juxtaposition.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The paired opposites of height and lowness, or rank and position.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A fixed contrast pair.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To lean, incline, or cause instability so that something gives way.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Suggests destabilizing displacement.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Audible sound as a collective pair, often referring to musical or spoken sound.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A paired expression for auditory phenomena.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To match, respond to, or agree in sound, feeling, or action.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Reciprocal agreement or resonance.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The paired positions or directions before and behind.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A fixed relational pair.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To come after or move along with something else.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Trailing or accompanying movement.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces a conclusion drawn from what precedes.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Inferential transition.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A person of exceptional wisdom, moral insight, and enlightened conduct.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In Daoist usage, an ideal ruler or exemplary person rather than a Confucian saint.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To remain in, take up, or deal with a matter or situation.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this context, to take up or manage a matter.
contextual_sense.Translation (English): to dwell; to handle; to manage

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): An action, matter, or thing that is done or dealt with.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A practical affair or matter, not an event in the abstract.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To move along or to put into practice.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means to practice or carry out.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Spoken language or verbal expression.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Oral expression, contrasted with silent teaching.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Guidance or doctrine given to others.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Instruction as something imparted or transmitted.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To come into activity, take action, or produce an effect.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Emergence into action or activity.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A locative or deictic element referring to a situation, place, or state already mentioned.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often marks location, state, or resultant circumstance.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To keep silent or not voice something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Refusal or abstention from speaking.
contextual_sense.Translation (English): to refuse to say; to be silent about

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To depend on something or hold it up as a support.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Dependence or self-support through something.
contextual_sense.Translation (English): to rely on; to take pride in

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The result, accomplishment, or merit of effort.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A completed beneficial result or achievement.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A literary negative form, often emphatic or formal in tone.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): More formal than 不.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To take up a position or keep oneself in a place or state.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Settled occupancy or retention.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): An exclamatory or introductory particle used to launch a statement or emphasis.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Discourse-opening or emphasis marker.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Restricts the statement to one factor or condition.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Exclusive or limiting only.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To go away or move off from a place or state.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Departure or removal.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To regard something as important, worthy, or high in status.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): To prize or set high value on.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A morally or socially capable person regarded as worthy of honor or office.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Someone esteemed for virtue or talent.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To bring about or let something happen.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Causative use.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The populace or common people as a collective.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): The general population, especially in governance contexts.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To compete, dispute, or struggle against another.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Conflict or competition for precedence.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To regard something as important, precious, or worth having.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): High valuation.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Not easy to do, obtain, or endure.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Difficulty of attainment or performance.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To acquire, reach, or gain possession of.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Successful acquisition or attainment.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Objects of value, especially commodities or possessions.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Valuable property or merchandise.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A person who steals or commits robbery.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Criminal who takes by stealth or force.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To perceive visually or to make something visible.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it is seeing or bringing into view.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The inner faculty of thought, feeling, and intention.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Psychological and moral interior, not the physical heart alone.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A state of confusion, turmoil, or lack of order.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Disordered state, whether moral, political, or emotional.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To administer a state or direct affairs with authority.
Sentence Translations (English): The king governs the state by virtue.
A good person can govern the people.
Harsh laws are hard to govern with.
First set oneself upright, and then govern others.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The act or institution of governing and administering public affairs.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Governance as a political order or practice.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Lacking contents or not occupied; vacant.
Sentence Translations (English): The room was empty and quiet.
His seat was already vacant.
Outwardly full, but inwardly empty.
If the heart can be empty, then it becomes clear.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To render something unfilled, less full, or devoid of what it previously had.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this context, to reduce or clear away inner content.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The inner seat of thought, feeling, intention, and awareness.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): The moral-psychological heart-mind rather than the physical organ alone.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To make something full or to supply it with what it needs.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Filling up or strengthening by supplying substance.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The stomach and lower trunk of the body.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Physical belly, often extended metaphorically to bodily nourishment.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To reduce strength, force, resolve, or intensity.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Causative weakening.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Inner intention, purpose, or determination.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Directed will or ambition.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To increase strength, firmness, or vigor.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Causative strengthening.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The hard parts of the body that support and give structure.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Literal bodily bone, often suggesting firmness.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A person who is intelligent or skillful in judgment, though not necessarily morally sage.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): One who has intelligence or practical understanding.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To have the courage or presumption to do something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Expresses boldness or permission by internal stance.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A final particle that marks cadence, emphasis, or completion in classical prose.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Softens or closes the statement.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces a consequence or logical result from the preceding condition.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Resultative or conditional consequence marker.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To become full or fill up to capacity.
Sentence Translations (English): The vessel gradually became full.
The spring vapors surged upward.

The boat moved on the water, as if the air were already full.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Lacking full substance or solid fullness; not densely packed.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Suggests openness and emptiness rather than emptiness as lack alone.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To employ something for a purpose or put it into service.
